policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: Genitive absolute vs. dative construction; both yield ASV 'And when he was come down from the mountain'. English cannot distinguish.
προσελθὼν and ἐλθὼν both render as 'there came to him'; the ASV shows no compound 'came to' vs 'came' distinction here. The lone note concerns the marginal note on worship at 2:2, not the participle.
ASV reads 'And he stretched forth his hand, and touched him' with a pronoun subject throughout; the added ὁ Ἰησοῦς of r01 would give a named subject 'Jesus touched him'.
Genitive absolute vs. dative; both yield 'And when he was entered into Capernaum'. English cannot distinguish.
ASV opens the verse 'And he saith unto him'; the ASV renders narrative καί with initial 'And', which the WH omission (asyndeton) would leave unrepresented.
ASV 'And he saith unto him' has a pronoun subject; the added ὁ Ἰησοῦς of r01 would give 'Jesus saith unto him'.

καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς and ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ both render 'And the centurion answered'; the ASV's initial 'And' fits either connective. The notes here are glosses and an alternative rendering, which do not decide a reading.

The ASV text has 'a man under authority' with no participle, and the mapped textual note 'Some ancient authorities insert set: as in Lk. 7:8' places τασσόμενος in the margin, i.e. outside the text rendered.

ASV text 'I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel' renders οὐδὲ ἐν τῷ Ἰσραὴλ τοσαύτην πίστιν εὗρον, and the mapped textual note assigns the base reading to the margin: 'Many ancient authorities read With no man in Israel have I found so great faith.'
ASV 'Go thy way; as thou hast believed, so be it done unto thee' renders no conjunction before 'as'; r01's καὶ ὡς would give 'and as thou hast believed'.
ASV reads 'the servant was healed', without the possessive that αὐτοῦ would require ('his servant').
ASV 'great multitudes' is plural with a quantifier, rendering πολλοὺς ὄχλους; r01's singular ὄχλον would give 'a multitude'.
ASV 'another of the disciples' lacks the possessive that αὐτοῦ would require ('his disciples').
ASV 'But Jesus saith unto him' is present tense, rendering λέγει; the aorist εἶπεν would give 'said'.
ASV 'when he was entered into a boat' is anarthrous; the added article τὸ would give 'the boat'.
ASV 'And they came to him, and awoke him' has an unexpressed pronoun subject; r01's οἱ μαθηταὶ would give 'the disciples came to him'.
ASV 'Save, Lord; we perish' has no object for the imperative; ἡμᾶς would give 'Save us, Lord'.
Word order only: αὐτῷ ὑπακούουσιν and ὑπακούουσιν αὐτῷ both render 'obey him'. English cannot distinguish.
Genitive absolute vs. dative; both yield 'And when he was come to the other side'. English cannot distinguish.
ASV names 'the country of the Gadarenes', transliterating Γαδαρηνῶν rather than r01's Γεργεσηνῶν ('Gergesenes').
ASV 'What have we to do with thee, thou Son of God?' has no vocative 'Jesus' that the added Ἰησοῦ would supply.
ASV 'send us away into the herd of swine' renders the imperative ἀπόστειλον with 'us' as its object; r01 ἐπίτρεψον ἡμῖν ἀπελθεῖν would give 'suffer us to go away'.
ASV 'went into the swine' renders τοὺς χοίρους alone; r01 τὴν ἀγέλην τῶν χοίρων would give 'into the herd of swine'.
ASV 'the whole herd rushed down the steep' has no qualifier; the added τῶν χοίρων would give 'the whole herd of swine'.
εἰς ὑπάντησιν and εἰς συνάντησιν are synonymous idioms both rendered 'to meet Jesus'. English cannot distinguish.
